body.text: 三個問題有設計上的依賴：先決定保護目標，再建立防護，最後透過授權測試評估效果。以下用診所、銀行與公司案例逐步推理。供稿保留題號、部分題意與選項說明，完整原題尚未全數提供；字母答案是供稿參考，不能據此宣稱已驗證正式題庫。

sections.heading: 第一章｜資訊安全在保護什麼？CIA

body.text: 1. 先從一個生活情境理解
假設你經營一家診所，診所使用電腦系統管理病歷。某天發生以下三件事：

items: 事件 A：一名陌生人偷偷讀取了病人的身分證字號、姓名、病史。
事件 B：一名員工不小心把病人的用藥劑量從 5 毫克改成 50 毫克。
事件 C：診所的資訊系統突然故障，醫師無法讀取病歷。
A：不應該看到資料的人，看到了嗎？
B：資料有沒有被不當修改？
C：需要使用資料的人，還能不能正常使用？

body.text: 這就是資訊安全最基本的三種保護目標。CIA 是 Confidentiality、Integrity、Availability 的縮寫：保密性、完整性與可用性。

body.name: cia
body.caption: CIA：資訊安全三要素
body.description: 這三項是資訊安全最基本的保護目標，也是 NIST 所採用的核心概念。三欄是平行目標，不是先後流程。

items.title: C · Confidentiality
items.body:
保密性
不該看的人不能看

items.title: I · Integrity
items.body:
完整性
資料必須正確可信

items.title: A · Availability
items.body:
可用性
需要時能正常使用

body.text: 這三個英文單字的安全定義，可回查 [NIST FIPS 199](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/fips/199/final)。接下來分別理解每個問題，再用案例判斷題幹的主要影響。
2. Confidentiality：保密性
Confidentiality 的意思是：只有被允許的人，才能取得受保護的資訊。想像你把銀行帳戶密碼寫在一張紙上；紙上的密碼沒有被修改，也沒有消失，但有人偷看了它。這就是保密性遭到破壞。
在電腦系統裡，常見的保密性問題包括：

items: 未授權的人讀取客戶資料。
網路封包中的敏感資訊被攔截並讀取。
公司將本應私密的文件錯誤設定為公開。
使用者將機密資料寄給錯誤的收件人。

rows: 不是所有人都能看的資訊
在資訊傳遞途中取得它
沒有經過適當加密保護、可以直接閱讀的內容
使用密碼學方法，讓沒有適當金鑰的人難以理解內容

body.text: 為什麼要加密？
假設你在網路上傳送一句虛構的教學文字：「我的銀行密碼是 123456」。未加密時，它是明文；使用適當的演算法與金鑰後，內容轉換為密文，再由持有適當金鑰的人依程序解密還原。

body.name: encryption
body.caption: 加密與解密：由明文到密文，再還原
body.description: 密文只示意呈現形式，並非實際加密計算結果。銀行密碼是虛構教學資料；實際加密另需適當模式與金鑰管理。

items.title: 原始資料：明文 Plaintext
items.body: 我的銀行密碼是 123456

items.title: 使用加密演算法與金鑰 → 密文 Ciphertext
items.body:
7F A2 9C 41 ...
示意字串，非實際加密結果

items.title: 使用適當金鑰解密
items.body: 還原原始內容

body.text: Encryption（加密）就像把信件放進只有合適鑰匙才能打開的保險箱。這個類比幫助理解存取限制；實際安全性仍取決於密碼方案、模式、金鑰管理與實作。
TLS（Transport Layer Security，傳輸層安全協定）是 HTTPS 等通訊協定使用的重要安全機制。正確實作與驗證時，它能保護傳輸中的資料機密性及完整性。不是所有資料加密都等於 TLS；用了 HTTPS，也不表示資料在所有儲存及處理環節都安全。
3. Integrity：完整性
Integrity 的意思是：資料不能被未經授權或不適當地修改、破壞。例如銀行系統原本記錄「存款餘額：100,000 元」，卻遭未經授權竄改成「存款餘額：900,000 元」。核心問題是資料已經不正確，而不是別人是否看到了資料。
先前筆記的血型案例也相同：病人的血型由 A 型被擅改成 B 型，即使沒有其他人偷看病歷，完整性仍已受損。

items: Tampering（竄改）：未經授權修改資料。
Hash（雜湊）：將資料轉換成固定長度摘要值的密碼學機制，常用來比對資料是否變動。
Digital Signature（數位簽章）：利用密碼學機制驗證資料來源與完整性，在適當條件下還能支持不可否認性。

body.text: 例如下載 Ubuntu ISO 映像檔後，計算檔案的 SHA-256，並與官方網站提供的摘要比較。兩者相同，可以提供檔案內容一致的強力證據；但 Hash 相同不代表檔案一定可信。
如果攻擊者同時替換檔案與網站上的 Hash 值，你仍可能被欺騙。因此，Hash 檢查內容是否一致；資料來源是否可信，還需要額外的認證機制。存取權限與變更稽核也可以共同保護完整性。
4. Availability：可用性
Availability 的意思是：有權使用系統的人，需要時能及時、可靠地使用。假設醫院沒有資料外洩，也沒有人改動病歷，但伺服器突然停止運作，醫師無法查詢用藥紀錄，這就是可用性問題。
先前掛號系統遭阻斷服務攻擊、醫師與病人無法登入的案例，也屬於可用性受損。資料可能未外洩、未被修改，服務仍已無法正常提供。

rows: 來自多個來源的大量攻擊流量
準備額外設備或系統，避免單點故障
保留資料副本以協助復原
重大事故後恢復服務的能力

body.text: 備份主要協助復原資料，不保證服務能立即恢復；系統備援與故障轉移更直接支援持續可用性。流量防護與災難復原也須依服務需求配置及驗證。
5. Non-Repudiation：不可否認性
供稿原題還有容易混淆的選項：Non-Repudiation（不可否認性）。假設甲公司與乙公司簽署電子合約，幾個月後，甲公司主張「這不是我們簽署的文件」。問題是：有人事後否認做過這件事，我們有什麼可靠證據可以判斷？
可信的數位簽章、金鑰管理、身分驗證與其他佐證，可支持某個行為確實出自特定簽署者。NIST 將簽章與資料來源認證、完整性及不可否認性連結，但不表示只要有簽章，就能在任何法律爭議中自動確定實際操作的人。
對照 [NIST FIPS 186-5](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/fips/186-5/final) 的簽章用途，再讀 [NIST 不可否認性定義](https://csrc.nist.gov/glossary/term/non_repudiation)，可看出技術驗證、金鑰歸屬與其他證據必須配合判讀。
6. 把四個名詞放在一起比較

rows: 有人否認自己簽署文件

body.text: 真實事件可能同時影響 CIA 多個面向。CEH 單選題通常要求根據題目最直接描述的安全問題，選擇最佳答案；分類是判斷工具，不會把複合事件硬分成互斥情況。
7. 回到供稿題號 P1-Q003
供稿描述一間律師事務所，以電子郵件傳送敏感法律文件。四段英文是主要線索：

items: sensitive legal documents：敏感法律文件。
clear text：以明文形式傳輸。
intercepting the traffic：攔截網路流量。
unauthorized individuals ... view：未經授權的人可以查看。
第一步：資料有沒有被修改？供稿題意沒有說。
第二步：系統有沒有不能使用？沒有這項描述。
第三步：有沒有身分或行為否認爭議？沒有。
第四步：資料是否有被未授權者讀取的風險？有，這正是重點。

body.text: 供稿參考答案為 B. Confidentiality。要學會的判斷原則是：當核心問題是未經授權取得資訊內容，優先思考保密性；不要只背「看到 clear text 就選 B」。完整原題與所有選項仍以實際題文核對。

sections.heading: 第二章｜安全控制與縱深防禦

body.text: 對應供稿題號 P3-Q113。本章先理解控制的用途，再分清實施形式、功能與縱深防禦。
1. 為什麼資訊安全不能只依靠防火牆？
想像一家公司的重要客戶資料都在機房。公司買了昂貴的防火牆，也裝了防毒軟體，某天卻有人直接走進機房，把伺服器硬碟帶走。問題在於防火牆主要管理網路流量，無法取代實體門禁。
Security Controls（安全控制）是組織為降低安全風險採取的保護措施。它可以是軟體、制度、一名保全或一把門鎖；NIST 的控制概念也包含技術、人員、管理與實體環境相關措施。
2. 安全控制的三種常見實施形式

rows: 以設施與現場人員保護建築、設備及場所
保全、門鎖、圍籬、門禁卡、機房出入管制
以軟硬體與技術機制保護系統
防火牆、防毒、加密、多因素驗證
以政策、流程、訓練與責任分工規範安全運作
資安教育訓練、帳號審核、存取權限政策

body.text: 這是 CEH 入門常見分類，不是所有標準唯一的分類方式。例如 NIST 文獻也有管理、作業與技術控制的分類；閱讀不同標準時，要先確認其分類軸。
3. 四個容易混淆的技術名詞

rows: 依規則允許或阻擋通訊
偵測與處理惡意程式的工具
將資料放進有密碼學保護的保險箱

body.text: 例如伺服器只需要對外提供 HTTPS，防火牆可允許必要通訊並阻擋不符合規則的連線。但正常 HTTPS 流量仍可能觸及有漏洞的網站程式，因此部署防火牆不等於網站程式已安全。
4. 什麼是縱深防禦？
假設把價值一億元的物品放進保險箱，合理設計不只是一把鎖：建築入口有門禁、內部有保全、重要區域需要額外驗證，保險箱另有獨立的鎖。第一道防線失效，攻擊者也不一定能直接取得物品。

body.name: defense
body.caption: 五層縱深防禦
body.description: 以機密資料系統為例。箭頭表示逐層閱讀，不表示所有攻擊都必須依序通過五層；各層共同處理不同失敗情況。

items.title: 第 1 層｜Physical
items.body: 保全、門禁與機房管制

items.title: 第 2 層｜Identity
items.body: 身分驗證、MFA 與權限限制

items.title: 第 3 層｜Network
items.body: 防火牆與網路區隔

items.title: 第 4 層｜Data
items.body: 加密、資料存取控制

items.title: 第 5 層｜Detection & Recovery
items.body: 監控、備份、復原與事件應變

body.text: MFA 是 Multi-Factor Authentication（多因素驗證），使用至少兩種不同類型的驗證因素，例如密碼加上實體安全金鑰。縱深防禦的重點是讓不同控制處理不同失敗情況，整合人員、技術與作業能力；產品數量多不自動代表防護有效。
5. 依功能分類：另一個判斷軸

rows: 發現正在發生或已發生的問題

body.text: 保全可以阻止未授權者進入，也可能發現可疑活動，因此同一措施能有多種功能。Physical 和 Preventive 不是互斥選項：前者描述如何實施，後者描述發揮什麼作用。
6. 回到供稿題號 P3-Q113
Which of the following is a "Physical" security control? 下列哪一項屬於實體安全控制？
供稿參考答案 C. Security Guard。辨識 Physical 時，思考現場人員、設施、實際進出與設備保護。

sections.heading: 第三章｜倫理駭客、授權與測試

body.text: 本章連接七筆倫理駭客、授權與安全測試目的的題號。Hacker 在不同時代與情境，可以指擅長理解、修改或探索技術系統的人，也常被用來指入侵者。
1. 工具相同，授權與目的仍可能不同
CEH 情境中的核心是目的、授權與實際行為。兩人使用同一工具測試公司網站：甲獲正式授權查漏洞；乙未經同意測試，並打算偷取客戶資料。工具相同，授權基礎與目的卻不同，不能用「會不會寫程式」或「用哪套工具」直接區分。
2. White Hat、Black Hat、Grey Hat

body.name: hats
body.caption: 白帽、黑帽與灰帽：先看授權與目的
body.description: 三列是角色比較，不是先後流程。動機、授權、實際行為與適用法律須一起判斷；帽子名稱不構成法律豁免。

items.title: White Hat（白帽駭客）
items.body:
在有效授權範圍內執行安全測試，目的是找出並改善安全問題。
例子：公司聘請資安顧問進行滲透測試。

items.title: Black Hat（黑帽駭客）
items.body:
通常為竊取、破壞或其他惡意目的，未經授權侵害系統。
例子：入侵公司資料庫，偷取客戶帳號。

items.title: Grey Hat（灰帽駭客）
items.body:
可能沒有直接惡意或獲利目的，卻在缺乏授權時測試。
例子：未經同意驗證網站漏洞，之後才通知站長。

body.text: 沒有惡意不自動代表合法。假設鄰居家門沒鎖，你覺得是在幫忙確認安全，就直接進屋查看，事後才告訴鄰居。出發點即使良善，也不會自動使進入他人住宅的行為合法；主動網路安全測試同樣需要確認授權。
Script Kiddie（腳本小子）主要依靠現成工具或攻擊程式，技術理解相對有限，描述的是能力或行為方式，不是與白帽／黑帽對等的授權分類。Blue Hat（藍帽）定義不一致，有時指受邀的外部測試者；它也不等於負責防禦的 Blue Team（藍隊）。題幹明確描述經授權測試、選項有 White Hat 時，通常優先判斷 White Hat。
3. Penetration Testing 是什麼？
Penetration Testing（Pentest，滲透測試）可從房屋安全檢查理解：屋主聘請專業人員，在約定條件下模擬入侵；檢查者除了指出窗戶容易打開，也可安全驗證弱點是否造成不當進入。電腦系統的滲透測試同樣是在授權範圍內模擬攻擊，驗證安全機制是否能被繞過。
NIST SP 800-115 的技術安全測試指引連接規劃、測試、分析與改善；測試成功突破不是工作終點，必須回到風險與修補。
4. 四個核心名詞與評估／測試的差別
假設銀行有錯誤設定，讓原應受限的資料被無權限者取得。將這個故事拆成以下四個元素：

rows: 需要保護的系統與資料
可能造成損害的行為者、事件或條件
透過弱點造成原本不應發生的結果

body.text: 弱點可能存在於軟體、系統程序、內部控制或實作，不只程式碼錯誤。Vulnerability Assessment（漏洞評估）著重辨識、分析、評估；Pentest 進一步在授權內確認能否被利用及其影響。兩者可交集，但重點不同。
例如掃描器發現軟體版本存在已知漏洞，仍要確認漏洞是否適用、是否可被利用；滲透測試可能進一步驗證實際安全影響。因此工具顯示有漏洞，不等於已證明系統成功遭入侵。
5. 授權不只是「老闆說可以」
Authorization 是某項操作獲得適當權限或許可。先確認誰有權允許、哪些系統與活動可測、何時可測、能用哪些方法，以及意外發生如何處理。董事長同意測公司雲端系統，不代表他能替第三方共享平台的其他廠商允許所有活動；授權人的權限與標的都必須確認。
6. Scope 與 ROE：測試界線
Scope（測試範圍）界定可測的系統、網域、IP、帳號或功能。Rules of Engagement（ROE，交戰規則）界定限制與操作程序；兩者互相關聯，但不是同一件事。以下是員工登入系統的虛構約定：

A 顛倒合法性；B 誤認兩者必用不同工具；D 誤以單人或團隊區分。這是本題最佳區別，實務還要判斷目的、範圍、法律與行為。

body.text: 情境：某醫療機構的資安測試
醫療機構委託外部資安公司測試，雙方簽署正式授權，範圍為病患預約系統。測試人員發現：

情況 C：缺乏足夠可用性保護，大量惡意請求可能中斷預約服務。
情況 D：另有醫療影像系統，但未列入範圍。
情況 E：機房設有防火牆，卻任何人都可直接進入。
1. A、B、C 分別主要影響 CIA 哪一項？為什麼？
2. 能直接對 D 的系統做滲透測試嗎？需要確認什麼？
3. E 暴露哪一類控制不足？建議哪些措施？

cards.question: 什麼條件讓滲透測試成為合乎規範的白帽行為？
answer: 先取得具有權限者的有效授權，明確約定測試目標、時段、方法限制與通報方式；在 Scope 與 ROE 內執行。
目標是識別、驗證漏洞並協助降低風險，留下報告與修補建議，再依約定複測。發現範圍外目標時，先停止該目標的主動測試，請求擴充授權。

cards.question: 病歷被偷看、血型被改壞、掛號系統無法使用，各影響 CIA 的哪一項？
answer: 未授權者偷看病歷：保密性（Confidentiality）。血型從 A 型被擅改為 B 型：完整性（Integrity）。掛號系統因阻斷服務無法使用：可用性（Availability）。
不可否認性關注行為證據與可歸責性，不是資料遭偷看最直接對應的目標。

cards.question: 為什麼有防火牆與加密，仍然需要保全和門禁？
answer: 保全與門禁保護實際場所和設備，屬於實體安全控制；防火牆與加密屬於技術控制；政策、授權程序與訓練屬於管理控制。
縱深防禦讓多種控制相互補強，涵蓋機房、人員、系統、資料及事件應變；任何單一控制都不能保證完全阻止攻擊。

body.text: 閱讀後，建議隔天、約三天後及一週後嘗試回憶；這些只是初始複習間隔，應依實際答題表現調整，不是固定適用所有人的遺忘曲線。

sections.heading: Chapter 1 | What does information security protect? CIA

body.text: 1. Start with an everyday scenario
Imagine that you run a clinic whose computer system manages medical records. One day, three incidents occur:

items: Incident A: a stranger secretly reads a patient's national ID number, name and medical history.
Incident B: an employee accidentally changes a patient's medication dose from 5 mg to 50 mg.
Incident C: the clinic information system suddenly fails, preventing doctors from reading records.
A: did someone who should not see the data gain access to it?
B: was the data improperly modified?
C: can the people who need the data still use it normally?

body.text: These are three fundamental information-security objectives. CIA abbreviates confidentiality, integrity and availability.

body.name: cia
body.caption: CIA: three information-security objectives
body.description: These are fundamental information-security objectives used by NIST. The three columns are parallel objectives, not sequential steps.

items.title: C · Confidentiality
items.body:
Confidentiality
People without permission must not see the data

items.title: I · Integrity
items.body:
Integrity
Data must remain correct and trustworthy

items.title: A · Availability
items.body:
Availability
Usable when needed

body.text: The security definitions are documented in [NIST FIPS 199](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/fips/199/final). Next, examine each objective and use scenarios to identify the main impact described by a question.
2. Confidentiality: controlling access to information

Confidentiality means that only permitted people can obtain protected information. Imagine writing a bank-account password on paper. The password is neither changed nor lost, but someone secretly reads it. Confidentiality has been compromised.
Common confidentiality problems in computer systems include:

items: An unauthorized person reads customer data.
Sensitive information in network packets is intercepted and read.
A company mistakenly makes a private document public.
A user sends confidential information to the wrong recipient.

rows: Information that not everyone is permitted to see
Not permitted to perform the activity
Making information available to another party
Acquire information while it is being transmitted
Content that can be read without suitable encryption protection
Makes content difficult to understand without the appropriate key

body.text: Why encrypt?

Suppose you transmit a fictional teaching sentence: “My bank password is 123456.” Without encryption it is plaintext. An appropriate algorithm and key transform it into ciphertext; someone with the appropriate key can follow the decryption procedure to recover the original.

body.name: encryption
body.caption: Encryption and decryption: plaintext, ciphertext and recovery
body.description: The ciphertext illustrates a representation, not an actual encryption result. The bank password is fictional teaching data. Real encryption also requires a suitable mode and key management.

items.title: Original data: plaintext
items.body: My bank password is 123456

items.title: Encryption algorithm and key → ciphertext
items.body:
7F A2 9C 41 ...
Illustrative bytes, not an actual encryption result

items.title: Decrypt using the appropriate key
items.body: Recover the original content

body.text: Encryption resembles putting a letter in a safe that opens only with a suitable key. The analogy explains access restrictions; actual security still depends on the cryptographic scheme, mode, key management and implementation.

TLS, Transport Layer Security, is an important security mechanism used by HTTPS and other protocols. Correct implementation and validation protect the confidentiality and integrity of data in transit. Data encryption is not always TLS, and HTTPS does not establish that every storage and processing stage is secure.
3. Integrity: preventing improper changes

Integrity means protecting data from unauthorized or improper modification or destruction. For example, a bank record showing “Balance: NT$100,000” is changed without authorization to “Balance: NT$900,000.” The central problem is incorrect data, rather than whether someone has read it.

The blood-type example from the previous notes illustrates the same principle: changing a patient record from type A to type B without authorization compromises integrity even if no one else reads the record.

items: Tampering: modifying data without authorization.
Hash: a cryptographic mechanism that maps data to a fixed-length digest, often used to check for changes.
Digital signature: a cryptographic mechanism for verifying data origin and integrity that can also support non-repudiation under appropriate conditions.

body.text: For example, after downloading an Ubuntu ISO image, calculate its SHA-256 digest and compare it with the digest provided by the official website. A match provides strong evidence of content consistency, but a matching hash does not by itself make the file trustworthy.

An attacker who replaces both the file and the published hash can still deceive you. A hash checks consistency; trusting the source requires additional authentication. Access controls and change-audit records can also contribute to integrity protection.
4. Availability: timely and reliable use

Availability means that authorized users can use a system promptly and reliably when needed. Suppose a hospital has no data leak or record modification, but its server suddenly stops and doctors cannot retrieve medication histories. This is an availability problem.

The earlier example of a denial-of-service attack preventing doctors and patients from logging into an appointment system also concerns availability. Service can fail even when data has neither leaked nor changed.

rows: Making a system unable to provide normal service
Large volumes of attack traffic from multiple sources
Extra equipment or systems to avoid a single point of failure
Recovering services after a major incident

body.text: Backups mainly support data recovery and do not guarantee immediate service restoration. Redundancy and failover more directly support continuing availability. Traffic protection and disaster recovery also need to be configured and verified against service requirements.
5. Non-repudiation: evidence when an action is denied

Another potentially confusing option in the supplied question is non-repudiation. Imagine that companies A and B sign an electronic contract. Months later, company A says, “We did not sign this document.” The question is what reliable evidence is available when someone later denies performing an action.

Trusted digital signatures, key management, identity verification and supporting evidence can help attribute an action to a particular signer. NIST connects signatures with data-origin authentication, integrity and non-repudiation; a signature does not automatically identify the actual operator in every legal dispute.

Compare the signature uses in [NIST FIPS 186-5](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/fips/186-5/final) with the [NIST definition of non-repudiation](https://csrc.nist.gov/glossary/term/non_repudiation). Technical verification, key attribution and other evidence must be assessed together.
6. Compare the four terms

rows: A bank balance is tampered with

body.text: A real incident may affect several CIA objectives. A CEH single-answer question usually asks for the best answer to the most directly described problem. The categories support judgment; they do not make complex incidents mutually exclusive.
7. Return to supplied reference P1-Q003
The supplied notes describe a law firm sending sensitive legal documents by email. Four English phrases provide the main clues:

items: sensitive legal documents: the content requires confidentiality.
clear text: the content travels in a readable form.
intercepting the traffic: another party can obtain traffic in transit.
unauthorized individuals ... view: people without permission may read the content.
Step 1: was data modified? That is not stated in the supplied scenario.
Step 2: is the system unavailable? No such condition is described.
Step 3: is there an identity dispute or denial of an action? No.
Step 4: could unauthorized people read the information? Yes; that is the central problem.

body.text: The supplied proposed answer is B, Confidentiality. The reusable principle is to think first about confidentiality when the core problem is unauthorized access to information content, rather than memorizing “clear text means B.” The complete original question and all options still require verification against the actual question text.

sections.heading: Chapter 2 | Security controls and defense in depth

body.text: Reference P3-Q113. First understand what controls do, then distinguish implementation categories, functions and defense in depth.
1. Why is a firewall insufficient on its own?

Imagine a company keeping important customer data in a server room. It buys an expensive firewall and installs antivirus software, but someone walks into the room and removes a server drive. A firewall primarily manages network traffic; it cannot replace physical access control.

Security controls are safeguards an organization uses to reduce security risk. A control can be software, a procedure, a guard or a lock. NIST also recognizes safeguards involving technology, people, management and the physical environment.
2. Three common implementation categories

rows: Facilities and on-site personnel protect buildings, equipment and locations
Guards, locks, fences, access cards and server-room restrictions
Hardware, software and technical mechanisms protect systems
Policies, procedures, training and assigned responsibilities guide secure operations
Security awareness training, account reviews and access policies

body.text: This is a common introductory CEH classification, not the only classification used by every standard. NIST publications also use management, operational and technical categories. Identify a standard’s classification axis before comparing its labels.
3. Four terms that are easy to confuse

rows: Allow or block communication according to rules
A tool to detect and handle malicious programs
A cryptographically protected safe for information
On-site control of people entering and leaving

body.text: For example, a server that only needs external HTTPS access can allow necessary traffic and block connections that violate its firewall rules. Permitted HTTPS traffic can still reach vulnerable application code, so deploying a firewall does not establish that the website application is secure.
4. What is defense in depth?

Suppose an item worth NT$100 million is stored in a safe. A reasonable design uses more than one lock: building access control, guards inside, extra verification for important areas and an independent safe lock. Failure of the first defense need not give an attacker direct access to the item.

body.name: defense
body.caption: Five layers of defense in depth
body.description: A confidential-data system example. Arrows indicate reading order, not a path every attack must follow. The layers address different failure conditions together.

items.title: Layer 1 | Physical
items.body: Security guards, access control and server-room restrictions

items.title: Layer 2 | Identity
items.body: Authentication, MFA and permission restrictions

items.title: Layer 3 | Network
items.body: Firewalls and network segmentation

items.title: Layer 4 | Data
items.body: Encryption and data access controls

items.title: Layer 5 | Detection & Recovery
items.body: Monitoring, backup, recovery and incident response

body.text: MFA, multi-factor authentication, uses at least two different types of authentication factors, such as a password and a physical security key. Defense in depth combines people, technology and operations so different controls address different failure conditions. A large product count does not automatically make protection effective.
5. Classification by function: a different axis

rows: Stop a problem before it occurs
Find a problem during or after its occurrence

body.text: A guard can prevent unauthorized entry and detect suspicious activity, so one control can serve several functions. Physical and preventive are not mutually exclusive: the former describes implementation, while the latter describes function.
6. Return to reference P3-Q113
Which of the following is a "Physical" security control? Identify the option that directly protects the physical environment.
The supplied proposed answer is C, Security Guard. For a physical-control question, think about on-site personnel, facilities, entry and exit, and equipment protection.

sections.heading: Chapter 3 | Ethical hacking, authorization and testing

body.text: This chapter connects seven references about ethical hacking, authorization and testing purposes. Depending on context and period, hacker can mean someone skilled at understanding, modifying or exploring technical systems, or can refer to an intruder.
1. The same tools can serve different authorization and purposes

In CEH scenarios, purpose, authorization and actual conduct are central. Two people use the same tool on a company website: one has formal permission to find vulnerabilities; the other lacks consent and intends to steal customer data. Their tools are the same, but authorization and purpose differ. Programming ability or tool choice alone does not distinguish their roles.
2. White hat, black hat and grey hat

body.name: hats
body.caption: White, black and grey hats: authorization and purpose
body.description: The rows compare roles, not consecutive steps. Consider motive, authorization, actual conduct and applicable law together; a hat label provides no legal exemption.

items.title: White hat
items.body:
Tests security within valid authorization to find and improve security problems.
Example: a company hires a security consultant for a penetration test.

items.title: Black hat
items.body:
Typically compromises systems without authorization for theft, damage or another malicious purpose.
Example: breaking into a company database to steal customer accounts.

items.title: Grey hat
items.body:
May lack a directly malicious or profit motive but tests without authorization.
Example: verifying a website vulnerability without consent, then notifying its owner.

body.text: Lack of malicious intent does not automatically establish legality. Imagine entering a neighbor’s unlocked house to check its security and only telling the neighbor afterward. A helpful intention does not automatically authorize entry; active network security testing likewise requires checking authorization.

Script kiddie describes someone relying mainly on ready-made tools or attack programs with limited technical understanding. It concerns skill or behavior rather than an authorization category equivalent to white or black hat. Blue hat has inconsistent definitions and sometimes means an invited external tester; it is not the same as the defensive blue team. Where a question explicitly describes authorized testing and offers white hat, that is usually the best match.
3. What is penetration testing?

Penetration testing, or pentesting, resembles a house-security inspection. The owner hires specialists to simulate intrusion under agreed conditions. They can identify a weak window and safely verify whether it permits improper entry. Computer pentesting similarly simulates attacks within authorization to evaluate whether security mechanisms can be bypassed.
NIST SP 800-115 connects planning, testing, analysis and mitigation. A successful bypass is not the end of the work; findings must inform risk decisions and remediation.
4. Four core terms and assessment versus testing
Suppose a bank misconfiguration exposes restricted data to someone without permission. Separate that scenario into four elements:

rows: A flaw that may be exploited
An actor, event or condition that may cause damage
Use a weakness to cause a result that should not be permitted

body.text: A vulnerability can occur in software, procedures, internal controls or implementation, not just source code. Vulnerability assessment emphasizes identifying, analyzing and evaluating weaknesses; pentesting further checks authorized exploitability and impact. The activities overlap but have different emphases.

For example, a scanner finding a software version associated with a known vulnerability still requires checking applicability and exploitability. A pentest may then verify actual impact. A vulnerability alert does not itself prove that a system has been successfully compromised.
5. Authorization requires more than “the boss said yes”

Authorization means receiving appropriate permission for an operation. Establish who can grant permission, which systems and activities are covered, when testing is allowed, permitted methods and incident procedures. A chairperson authorizing tests of company cloud systems may not have authority to permit every activity on a third-party shared platform. Both the grantor’s authority and the target matter.
6. Scope and ROE: testing boundaries

Scope defines the systems, domains, IP addresses, accounts or functions included in testing. Rules of engagement, or ROE, define restrictions and operating procedures. They are related but distinct. The following is a fictional agreement for an employee-login system:

body.name: roe
body.caption: Fictional example: penetration-testing agreement
body.description: 192.0.2.0/24 is reserved for documentation and teaching. The neighboring 192.0.2.11 does not automatically enter the authorized scope.

items.title: Scope
items.body: The 192.0.2.10 server

items.title: Testing time
items.body: Saturday, 10:00–14:00

items.title: Permitted methods
items.body: The specified security-verification activities

items.title: Prohibited activities
items.body: DoS, unauthorized data deletion and out-of-scope access

items.title: Incident reporting
items.body: Immediately report system abnormalities to the designated contact

body.text: Discovering a suspected vulnerability at neighboring 192.0.2.11 does not permit testing it opportunistically. Check the scope and obtain a formal change when needed. 192.0.2.0/24 is reserved for documentation. ROE are established before testing and authorize defined activities, not unrestricted operations.

The supplied proposed answer to P3-Q124 is C, Always obtain written permission before testing. Written authorization supports risk management and evidence, but it must still be valid, cover the actual activities and comply with applicable law.
7. The purpose of ethical hacking
Bypassing a system is one possible way to verify risk. The purpose is to help an organization understand and address weaknesses. These five steps connect authorization, discovery and improvement:

body.name: testing
body.caption: From security testing to risk reduction
body.description: The five steps connect in order. The responsible team remediates findings, followed by retesting. Finding no vulnerability in one test does not establish complete security.

items.title: Obtain authorization
items.body: Confirm which systems and activities may be tested

items.title: Find weaknesses
items.body: Identify potential security vulnerabilities

items.title: Verify impact
items.body: Determine within the agreed limits whether a weakness is exploitable

items.title: Report findings
items.body: Explain evidence, impact and remediation recommendations

items.title: Remediate and retest
items.body: The responsible team fixes the issue, then verifies whether the improvement works

body.text: For EC-Q331, the supplied answer is B, To identify and fix security vulnerabilities in a system. Fix means enabling remediation and security improvement; the tester does not necessarily modify the application personally. Remediation by the responsible team still needs retesting.

sections.heading: Chapter 5 | Reasoning through nine references

body.text: Apply the principles to the nine references. The following retains the supplied key wording and option reasoning. These are the supplied expected answers; missing complete question texts still need verification.
EC-Q001
Question clue: full knowledge and permission from the organization
Supplied proposed answer: D. White Hat Hacking
The company knows and permits the pentest. Blue hat has inconsistent definitions; grey hat does not match explicit authorization, and black hat conflicts with the authorized testing purpose.
Question clue: clear text ... intercepting the traffic ... read the contents
Supplied proposed answer: B. Confidentiality
Legal documents travel in cleartext and may be read without permission. Availability concerns usability, integrity concerns improper changes, and non-repudiation concerns evidence against denial.
Question clue: Physical security control
Supplied proposed answer: C. Security Guard
The question concerns implementation category. Firewall, antivirus and encryption are primarily technical; guards control entry into physical locations.
EC-Q054
Question clue: full knowledge and permission
Supplied proposed answer: C. White Hat
Almost the same concept as EC-Q001 with reordered options. Remember authorization conditions, not whether white hat appears as C or D.
Question clue: main ethical rule
Supplied proposed answer: C. Always obtain written permission before testing

A, gaining access by any means, ignores authorization boundaries. B, selling vulnerabilities on the dark web, is not the responsible testing purpose. D, withholding notification from affected owners, conflicts with appropriate reporting.
EC-Q166
Question clue: hired to legally assess ... identifying vulnerabilities and attempting to exploit them
Supplied proposed answer: D. White Hat

Being hired to lawfully assess and verify vulnerabilities matches white hat. Grey hat does not match explicit authorization; black hat is not the lawful testing role; script kiddie describes skill or tool reliance.
EC-Q189
Question clue: main difference between ethical hacking and malicious hacking
Supplied proposed answer: C. Ethical hacking is performed with permission, while malicious hacking is unauthorized

A reverses the authorization distinction. B incorrectly assumes different tools. D incorrectly uses solo versus team work to distinguish roles. This is the best distinction in the question; practice also requires assessing purpose, scope, law and conduct.
EC-Q331
Question clue: primary goal of ethical hacking
Supplied proposed answer: B. To identify and fix security vulnerabilities in a system
A, disrupting service; C, stealing information; and D, spreading malware are not the legitimate primary purpose. Fix includes enabling remediation by the responsible team.
EC-Q476
Question clue: role of a penetration tester
Supplied proposed answer: C. Authorized security professional who exploits vulnerabilities
Authorized is decisive. Exploits here means verifying weaknesses within authorization, not unrestricted attack.
The nine references repeatedly test a few principles. Develop reusable reasoning rather than treating them as nine isolated answers.

sections.heading: Chapter 7 | Combined medical-institution scenario

body.text: Scenario: testing a medical institution
A medical institution hires an external security company and signs formal authorization covering the patient-appointment system. The testers find:

items: A: patient contact details travel without suitable encryption and may be read by a third party.
B: an authorization-check flaw may let unauthorized people change appointment times.
C: insufficient availability protection means heavy malicious requests may interrupt appointments.
D: another medical-imaging system exists but is outside scope.
E: the server room has a firewall, but anyone can physically enter.
1. Which CIA objective is primarily affected by A, B and C, and why?
2. May the testers directly pentest D? What must they confirm?
3. Which control category is deficient in E, and what would you recommend?
4. What information must a report contain to support practical improvement?
5. Can fixing known vulnerabilities establish “complete security”? Explain.

body.text: Write your reasoning as answers 1–5; this is not automatically graded. The questions connect objectives, authorization and controls rather than English memorization. A teacher or peer can review the reasoning, address gaps and retest using another scenario.
The principles are checked against sources including NIST FIPS 199, SP 800-115 and SP 800-53. That does not make these new scenario exercises official CEH questions.

sections.heading: Supplement | Three recall cards from the prior edition

body.text: Do not treat the nine references as nine unrelated facts to memorize. Seven concern ethical hacking, valid authorization and risk reduction; the other two concern confidentiality and physical security controls. The source originally says “six” here; counting the references in the table gives seven.

Organize the content into three active-recall cards. First explain the answer yourself, then reveal the reference answer and check its conditions and reasoning. The first prompt and its references follow the supplied image; the other two prompts and all three answers are completed from the article content.

body.caption: Active Recall
body.description: Answer in your mind before revealing the answer. Viewing or revealing a card supports review; it does not establish understanding or exam readiness.

cards.question: What conditions make a penetration test a properly authorized white-hat activity?
answer: Obtain valid authorization from someone with the authority to grant it. Agree on targets, testing times, method restrictions and notifications, then work within the scope and ROE.

Identify and validate vulnerabilities to help reduce risk, provide a report and remediation recommendations, and retest as agreed. For an out-of-scope target, stop active testing of that target and request expanded authorization.

cards.question: Which CIA objective is affected by exposed records, an altered blood type and an unavailable registration system?
answer: Unauthorized viewing of records affects confidentiality. Changing blood type A to B without authorization affects integrity. A registration system disabled by denial of service affects availability.
Non-repudiation concerns evidence of actions and accountability; it is not the direct objective affected by unauthorized viewing.

cards.question: Why are guards and door access controls still needed when firewalls and encryption are in place?
answer: Guards and door access controls protect physical spaces and equipment and are physical controls. Firewalls and encryption are technical controls. Policies, authorization procedures and training are administrative controls.
Defense in depth combines protections for facilities, people, systems, data and incident response. No single control guarantees that every attack is prevented.

options: A. Test B as long as your intention is to help the company
B. Stop active testing of B and request expanded authorization
C. Using free tools means the test does not violate authorization

B is outside the current scope. Stop active testing of B and obtain valid expanded authorization before proceeding.

options: A. Confidentiality
B. Integrity
C. Availability
rationales: Confidentiality concerns unauthorized disclosure; the scenario says there was no unauthorized viewing.
Unauthorized changes to account balances directly compromise data integrity.
Availability concerns using a service when needed; the scenario does not describe an outage.

items.prompt: A company uses encryption and firewalls, but anyone can enter its server room. Which type of security control is most directly missing?
options: A. Physical
B. Cryptographic
C. Network
rationales: Unrestricted access to the server room most directly calls for physical security controls.
Encryption protects data but does not directly stop people entering the room.
Network controls protect network access and cannot replace guards or door access controls.

body.text: The central relationship in this M01 practice is: authorization determines whether you may test; CIA identifies what you protect; security controls describe how you protect it. Use this relationship to reason through other CEH scenarios.

items: Permission：合法授權與測試邊界。

body.text: 1. 為什麼資安需要多種技術？
想像你管理醫院資安：醫師登入病歷系統、病人上網查資料，院方也定期委託漏洞測試。每天面對的不是單一「有沒有被駭」問題，而是授權、風險、監控、營運、清除、加密與信任等問題。原稿「醫院的七個安全問題」圖的細部節點未隨文字提供；以下依已提供的五單元表完整承接其知識架構。

保密性
不該看的人不能看

sections.heading: 單元一｜White Hat 與合法授權

body.text: 對應 EC-Q535，連回 M01-03 倫理駭客、授權與交戰規則。
1. 鎖匠與小偷可能用相同技術
屋主聘請鎖匠測門鎖，鎖匠用工具打開後提出更換建議，屬於約定內安全測試。另一人未取得同意，用同工具開門，即使聲稱只是證明不安全，也不能只憑動機判斷合法。同一技術行為要放回授權、目的與實際行為條件。
2. 專有名詞逐一理解

主要使用他人現成攻擊工具
描述熟練度，不是授權類型

5. 變化練習：私下回報不取代授權
研究員未經同意主動測網站，最後私下回報，不能只因沒有惡意就認定 White Hat。應追問是否有授權、公開揭露政策是否允許這種活動、是否越過合法範圍。能提出這些問題，才掌握此題原理。

sections.heading: 單元二｜ISO、SOC 與營運持續

body.text: 對應 P1-Q063、P3-Q086、P3-Q088：先了解風險、平常監控分流、出事時維持必要業務。它們相互協作，分別是管理指引、營運職責與持續計畫。

5. SOC 與初步分流
SOC（Security Operations Center，資安維運中心／安全營運中心）像急診分流：第一線先判斷緊急程度，需深入處理才交適當團隊。大量登入失敗、可疑連線與惡意程式警報，不能每筆都由最資深專家深查。
Monitoring 是持續觀察活動，例如反覆嘗試登入管理員帳號；Triage 是判斷警報重要性、可信度與是否升級。分流不代表已完整證實攻擊，也不要求 Tier 1 獨自處理所有漏洞。

body.text: 對應 P3-Q110，先分清 Delete、資料復原與媒體安全清除。
1. 從圖書館目錄理解 Delete
館員刪掉一本書的目錄，讀者搜尋不到，書卻可能仍在架上。檔案刪除也可能只是移除檔案或其參照，並不等於所有底層資料已安全清除。實際效果受檔案系統、裝置、TRIM 與加密影響，不能假設刪除後一定能復原或一定不能復原。
2. Data Recovery 為何也是風險？
Data Recovery（資料復原）嘗試取回誤刪、檔案系統損壞或設備故障後的資料，可能利用殘留內容、檔案系統資訊、備份或其他副本。對使用者有用，對準備報廢的敏感資料設備卻是風險：醫院賣掉存過檢驗報告的舊電腦，不能只靠刪檔就認定符合清除要求。
3. Clear、Purge、Destroy
NIST SP 800-88 Rev. 2 在 2025 年 9 月發布，區分三種 Media Sanitization（媒體資料清除）方法。

rows: 阻止透過一般使用者介面，以簡單非侵入方式復原

使實驗室等級復原不可行，也使媒體無法再儲存資料

body.text: 4. Purge 為何不等於砸壞硬碟？
Purge 是方法與保證目標的分類，不是固定動作。適當裝置清除功能或可靠 Cryptographic Erase（加密抹除）可能達成：資料原先充分加密，安全消除所有必要解密金鑰後，原密文失去可行的還原途徑。就像已用可靠鎖具保護的內容，消除所有可用鑰匙後難以開啟。

items: 資料自最近一次適當清除後即受適當加密，不曾遺留以明文寫入的敏感內容。

sections.heading: 單元四｜加密、區塊、金鑰與分配

body.text: 對應 EC-Q284、EC-Q032，連回 M20 對稱／非對稱密碼學。先問加密是什麼、金鑰是什麼、如何處理資料、雙方如何取得共同秘密。
1. 為什麼加密？演算法與金鑰的分工
醫院 A 將檢驗報告傳給醫院 B，希望 B 看得懂、未授權第三人看不懂。Encryption 將明文轉成密文，Decryption 以適當金鑰等資訊還原；對稱加密的基本關係是「明文＋加密程序與秘密金鑰 → 密文 → 解密程序與相應秘密金鑰 → 明文」。實際還涉及 IV、Nonce、運作模式與認證標籤。

rows: 以適當金鑰等資訊還原

body.text: Algorithm（演算法）像鎖的設計，Key（金鑰）像控制這把鎖的特定秘密設定。現代密碼學應在攻擊者知道演算法、卻缺乏秘密資訊時仍難以破解，因此公開演算法不等於不安全。
2. 對稱加密與金鑰分配問題
Symmetric Encryption 使用雙方共享的秘密金鑰，或可相應使用的秘密材料。就像你用共同密碼加密、同事以相同密碼解密。它通常適合快速處理資料庫、儲存與網路的大量資料，但雙方原本沒共享秘密時，不能直接在不安全管道傳金鑰；這就是 Key Distribution Problem。
3. Bit、Byte、Block 與 Key Size
Bit 的值是 0 或 1；一 Byte 通常為 8 bits。64 bits = 8 bytes，128 bits = 16 bytes。Block 是一次加密轉換的固定資料單位，Block Size 是該單位的位元數；Key Size 則是金鑰長度，兩者不是同一個量。
一次處理 8 bytes 的演算法有 64-bit 區塊。8,000 bytes 的檔案需由適當模式分段，並按模式規定處理末段；不是整個檔案只能有一個區塊。Blowfish 無論用 32–448-bit 哪種金鑰，區塊仍為 64 bits；AES 區塊為 128 bits。
類比：Block Size 像機器一次能加工多大的材料；Key Size 像秘密設定有多少可能組合。兩者都重要，類比只幫助區分用途。
4. Block Cipher 與 Stream Cipher
Block Cipher 對固定長度資料區塊轉換，例如 AES、Blowfish、Twofish。Stream Cipher 產生金鑰串流等機制連續處理資料，例如 RC4、ChaCha20。明確看到 64-bit blocks，先找符合區塊長度的區塊加密，不選串流加密。
5. 四種演算法的規格
Bruce Schneier 在 1993 年提出 Blowfish；其設計頁記錄 64-bit 區塊、32–448-bit 金鑰。Twofish 則採 128-bit 區塊。NIST FIPS 197 指定 AES 三種金鑰長度，但三者區塊都為 128 bits。
6. 解 EC-Q284：找區辨力最大的特徵
金融公司、外洩、攔截密文與安全儲存是背景；關鍵為 processes data in 64-bit blocks 與 supports a variable key size from 32 to 448 bits。

items: RC4 是串流加密，排除。
Twofish 是 128-bit 區塊，排除。
AES 是 128-bit 區塊，金鑰也不是 32–448 bits，排除。
Blowfish 同時符合兩特徵；供稿答案 D。

body.text: DES 替代方案是合理歷史背景，但不是唯一辨識依據。實際只拿到密文，通常不能自動知道演算法；還需協定協商、程式設定、檔案格式等證據。
7. 金鑰較長不代表整體一定較安全
均勻隨機的 128-bit 金鑰有 2^128 種可能，每增加 1 bit，組合數翻倍，影響 Brute Force（暴力破解）的搜尋空間。但安全還取決於區塊、模式、數學弱點、產生金鑰方式與實作；不能只比較 Blowfish 448 與 AES 256。
8. Birthday Bound 與 64-bit 區塊
一年有 365 個生日，23 人中卻已有超過約 50% 的機率出現同生日，稱 Birthday Paradox（生日悖論）。類似碰撞機率讓某些模式在同一金鑰下處理約 2^32 個 64-bit 區塊時，風險需要特別注意。
每區塊 8 bytes，所以 2^32 × 8 bytes = 34,359,738,368 bytes，約 34.4 GB（32 GiB）。這不是跨過門檻就必然立即洩密；實際攻擊取決於模式、金鑰使用與其他條件。2016 Sweet32 展示特定 TLS／OpenVPN 與 CBC 條件下的攻擊，不能推廣成所有加密的固定安全用量。
Mode of Operation（運作模式）規定如何用區塊演算法處理長訊息，例如 CBC、CTR、GCM。AEAD（Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data，附加資料認證加密）在正確使用下結合保密性、完整性與附加資料認證。AES 是核心演算法，AES-GCM 是結合特定模式的方案。新設計不能只因 Blowfish 金鑰長就忽略其小區塊限制。
9. 公鑰、私鑰、ECDHE 與 KDF
Asymmetric Cryptography（非對稱密碼學）使用有數學關係的 Public Key（公鑰，可公開）與 Private Key（私鑰，須保護）。對支援公開金鑰加密的方案，Alice 可取得可信的 Bob 公鑰加密，再由 Bob 私鑰解密；不是所有非對稱演算法都能加密文件，也不建議因此直接處理大型檔案。
ECDHE（暫時性橢圓曲線 Diffie–Hellman）讓雙方公開交換資訊，各自計算共享秘密，不直接傳送該秘密。這是 Key Agreement（金鑰協議）；再經 KDF（Key Derivation Function，金鑰導出函數）產生 Session Key（工作階段金鑰），由對稱式機制保護大量資料。
所以常見混合分工為「公鑰技術建立秘密 → KDF 導鍵 → 對稱機制保護資料」。對稱通常更適合大量資料，公鑰機制則承擔金鑰建立、簽章等任務，不必全程直接用公開金鑰加密。
10. 解 EC-Q032：金鑰分配
Which encryption method supports secure key distribution? 題目問哪類方法支援安全金鑰分配。

3. Hash 檢查變動的條件
醫院透過可信管道提供檢驗報告 SHA-256，收到檔案後重算。不同表示資料或計算條件有差異；相同在安全假設與可信原摘要前提下，提供強力一致性證據。Hash 不會阻止修改；若攻擊者連文件與網站摘要一起換掉，單純比對可能發現不了。
4. HMAC：需要共享秘密的認證碼
HMAC（Hash-based Message Authentication Code）將雜湊與共享秘密金鑰結合。普通 Hash 誰都能算；HMAC 需持有秘密才能產生有效認證碼。例如醫院 A 以共享金鑰計算，醫院 B 以同一金鑰驗證；不知道金鑰的攻擊者不能只改資料、重算普通 Hash 就取得有效 HMAC。
NIST FIPS 198-1 說明這個定義；其網站另有遷移內容至 SP 800-224 的規劃提示。共享金鑰的雙方都能產生 HMAC，所以單靠 HMAC 不能證明究竟是哪個持有者發送。這是它與可公開驗證簽章的重要差別。
5. Digital Signature：私鑰簽署、公鑰驗證
數位簽章提供訊息完整性，以及對應公鑰之私鑰持有者的簽署證據。概念流程是「資料 → 簽章方案內的摘要／編碼等處理 → 私鑰簽署 → 傳送資料與簽章」；接收者以可信公鑰及指定方案驗證。具體程序依演算法，不能概括成把 Hash 用私鑰加密。

7. PKI：光有 Public Key 還不夠
銀行說「這是我的公鑰」，攻擊者也能產生金鑰並冒稱銀行。需要制度把公鑰與特定身分或網域可信綁定。PKI（Public Key Infrastructure，公開金鑰基礎建設）包含公開金鑰憑證、CA、信任錨點與管理／驗證程序。
8. CA：憑證核發者
CA（Certificate Authority，憑證機構）像證件核發單位：公司申請網站憑證，CA 依政策驗證資訊並簽發。憑證含公鑰、適用身分資訊、期限、簽發者及簽章等；CA 簽章讓瀏覽器依信任政策驗證簽發鏈。
9. Certificate Chain：從根到網站

rows: 由上層授權簽發的中繼機構

body.text: 常見 Web PKI 的根集合由瀏覽器或作業系統維護，實際鏈可能不同層數。驗證不只是「有 CA 簽名」，還檢查鏈、名稱、期限、用途與限制。公開信任憑證不保證公司合法經營、內容安全或沒有惡意程式；信任範圍是特定身分與金鑰關係。
10. HTTPS 如何組合這些機制？
HTTPS 是 TLS 保護的 HTTP。常見憑證式 TLS 1.3 結合 ECDHE 等非對稱金鑰建立、CA 憑證與伺服器認證、KDF 導鍵及 AES-GCM 等對稱 AEAD；以下保留兩端、訊息方向與本機驗證責任。

cards.question: 白帽和黑帽的主要差別，是不是會不會用攻擊工具？
answer: 不是。相同工具可用在不同授權、目的與行為下；先確認有效授權與界線。

cards.question: ISO/IEC 27001、27002、27005 如何區分？
answer: 27001 是 ISMS 要求，27002 是控制指引，27005 是風險管理指引。後兩者都可支援前者，不是固定先後流程。

cards.question: 為什麼一般 Delete 不能直接視為 Purge？
answer: 刪除可能只移除檔案參照。Purge 要在合適裝置方法與驗證下，讓先進實驗室復原目標資料不可行。

cards.question: Blowfish 的 64-bit 與 448-bit 分別是什麼？
answer: 64 bits 是區塊大小；448 bits 是支援的最大金鑰長度。增加金鑰不會把區塊變大。

cards.question: 為什麼現代 TLS 常同時需要非對稱與對稱密碼學？
answer: 憑證式 ECDHE 連線用公鑰技術建立秘密與認證，再以 KDF 導鍵、對稱 AEAD 保護大量資料；仍須正確驗證對象。

cards.question: 為何普通 SHA-256 摘要不能單獨證明未被惡意修改？
answer: 攻擊者若同時替換資料與摘要，比對仍會一致；需可信參考摘要或適當的 MAC、簽章等認證。

cards.question: PKI 中 CA 與 Browser 的工作差在哪？
answer: CA 依政策驗證申請並簽發憑證；Browser 在連線時依信任政策驗證鏈、名稱、期限與相關條件。

body.text: 單元 1｜什麼時候駭客是在合法協助？（第 10 題）
1. 白話解釋：想像你請鎖匠測試門鎖
你請鎖匠試著打開你家的門，目的是確認門鎖是否安全。
鎖匠成功打開門，代表你發現了安全漏洞；但因為他有你的授權，而且依照約定測試，所以這是一項合法的安全檢查。
假如同一位鎖匠沒有經過鄰居同意，就跑去測試鄰居家的門鎖，即使只是為了提醒對方有安全問題，也不會自動變成合法行為。
最關鍵的差異不是技術，而是授權、範圍與行為。
2. 正式定義
White Hat Hacker（白帽駭客）是經授權、為改善安全而進行測試的安全研究或測試人員。
在組織環境中，通常涉及兩個重要文件或約定：

items: Authorization：正式授權。
Rules of Engagement（ROE）：交戰規則，規範允許的測試目標、時間、技術、限制與應變程序。

真正成熟的組織會同時問兩個問題：
「我們能不能阻止攻擊擴大？」與「即使攻擊還沒處理完，最重要的服務能不能繼續？」
只關注第一個問題，可能讓技術團隊成功隔離了攻擊，卻沒有為臨床工作建立可行的替代流程。
單元 3｜Delete、Clear、Purge、Destroy 到底有何不同？（第 11 題）
1. 白話解釋：你把文件丟進垃圾桶，真的不見了嗎？
想像有四種做法：
第一種是移除資料的目錄記錄，就像把一本書從圖書館索引中刪除，但書可能仍在架上。
第二種是以適當的方法清除資料，讓一般介面難以恢復。
第三種採取更強的資料消除方法，讓具有先進實驗室技術的人也無法在可行成本內復原。
第四種則是把保存資料的媒體實際銷毀。
這四種方式的保證程度不同。
2. 正式定義
NIST SP 800-88 Rev. 2《Guidelines for Media Sanitization》於 2025 年 9 月 26 日正式發布，取代 2014 年的 Rev. 1。這是本題應採用的重要現行參考。

body.text: 3. 運作原理：Purge 強調的是復原不可行性
NIST 對 Purge 的定義，強調使用物理或邏輯技術，使目標資料無法透過現有最先進的實驗室方法可行地復原。
這不代表每台硬碟都可以使用同一種清除指令。
硬碟、SSD、USB 隨身碟與其他儲存媒體的內部運作差異很大，例如 SSD 有 Flash Translation Layer（FTL）及備用儲存區，單純覆寫使用者可見的磁區，不一定涵蓋所有原始資料位置。
另外一種重要技術是 Cryptographic Erase（CE，加密抹除）。
假設整個儲存媒體的資料原本就使用適當的金鑰加密，且能安全地清除所有必要的解密金鑰，便可能達到所需的資料清除目標。但是否符合 Purge，仍需確認加密實作、金鑰副本、媒體支援與清除驗證等前提。
4. 實際案例
醫院要將存放病歷資料的 SSD 移交給外部回收廠商。
資訊人員只按作業系統的「刪除檔案」，並不能證明病歷資料已安全消除。
正確決策必須先確認資料敏感程度、媒體類型、是否要重用、可支援的清除方法，接著執行、驗證並留存紀錄。若媒體無法可靠清除，且不需要重用，可能需要選擇適當的物理銷毀。
5. 比較與區別
請記住，Purge 不等於 Destroy。
Purge 通常希望媒體仍可重用，但原始資料已不可行地復原；Destroy 則使媒體失去原本的儲存用途。
而且安全清除的範圍不能只包含主磁碟。如果資料另存於 Snapshot、Backup、其他儲存節點或外部備份，也需要獨立管理。
最佳答案是 B. To make data recovery impossible even with laboratory-grade tools.
但題目中的 impossible 不夠精確。考試意圖是「即使使用實驗室級技術也難以復原」，正式標準則使用 infeasible（不可行）這個概念。
A 只是刪除檔案指標，C 是硬體回收而非清除定義，D 是資料封存，與銷毀目的相反。
7. 進階補充
對實務決策來說，不要只問「我用了什麼清除工具」，還要問：
「這個工具是否真的對該媒體及該資料範圍有效？有沒有驗證證據？」
NIST Rev. 2 特別強調組織層級的媒體清除管理、方法適用性及對廠商實作的信任評估，而非只列出一組固定的硬碟覆寫指令。
單元 4｜對稱式加密與非對稱式加密（第 15、16 題）
1. 白話解釋：加密就像把資料鎖進保險箱
想像你要將一份機密報告傳給同事。
你可以用一把鑰匙鎖住保險箱，讓同事使用同一把鑰匙開啟。這類似對稱式加密（Symmetric Encryption）。
但新的問題出現了：
你要如何安全地把鑰匙交給同事？
如果你直接在不安全的網路上傳送鑰匙，攻擊者可能先偷到鑰匙，再打開保險箱。
這就是公開金鑰密碼學（Public-Key Cryptography）要協助解決的問題之一。

3. 運作原理：Block Size 不等於 Key Size
這是第 15 題最重要的技術觀念。
假設有一個區塊加密演算法，每次處理 64 bits（8 bytes）的資料。
我們說它的 Block Size = 64 bits。
而加密金鑰可以有不同長度，這稱為 Key Size。
Block Size 決定演算法一次處理多少位元；Key Size 影響金鑰空間與暴力猜測的難度，但並非評估安全性的唯一因素。

body.text: Blowfish 的特徵由原設計者 Bruce Schneier 的文件確認；Twofish 及 AES 的規格也可分別由原設計資料和 NIST FIPS 197 查證。
這裡有一個重要的安全問題。
假設 Blowfish 使用 256-bit 金鑰，你可能會認為金鑰已經非常長，因此一切都安全。
但 64-bit 區塊長度仍然可能造成生日界限（Birthday Bound）相關風險。在某些模式與大量資料使用情境下，約 2^{32} 個區塊的規模就需要特別注意碰撞問題。
Sweet32 研究展示了 64-bit 區塊加密在特定長連線及協定條件下的攻擊風險。這個問題不會因為將 Blowfish 金鑰從 128 bits 增加至 448 bits 就自動消失。

body.text: 6. 回到兩道考題
EC-Q284 → D. Blowfish。
決定性線索是「64-bit 區塊」以及「32–448-bit 可變金鑰」。Twofish、AES 的區塊都是 128 bits，RC4 則不是區塊加密。
題目中的「DES 替代品」是輔助線索，不能單靠這個描述判斷，因為多種演算法都曾被設計或評估作為 DES 的替代方案。
另有一個題幹推論限制：真實情況下，通常無法僅憑截取的一段密文，就直接確認使用的演算法。還需要協定資訊、實作紀錄或其他證據。
EC-Q032 → D. Asymmetric Encryption。
四個選項中，只有非對稱密碼學最符合安全金鑰分配或建立的概念。
Disk Encryption 是使用場景，Symmetric Encryption 需要預先處理共享金鑰問題，Hash Functions 則不是用來將可解密的金鑰安全傳送給對方。
7. 進階補充
現代 TLS 1.3 可以使用 ECDHE 建立共享祕密，再導出傳輸金鑰，使用 AES-GCM 等 AEAD（Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data）演算法保護資料。
此外，2026 年 7 月發布的 RFC 9846 已取代原本的 RFC 8446，成為 TLS 1.3 的更新規範。它保留 TLS 1.3 的主要架構，並收緊若干安全要求，包括禁止在不同連線間重複使用 KeyShare 值。
因此，真正安全的密碼學系統，不只取決於演算法名稱，還包括金鑰管理、身分驗證、模式與實作細節。

第二，這份合約是不是真的由你發出的？
這其實是兩個不同問題。
Hash 可以幫助檢查內容是否一致，但單純的 Hash 無法證明發送者身分。
如果需要驗證內容來源，就必須再加入共享祕密金鑰或數位簽章等機制。

items: Preimage Resistance：給定摘要，計算上難以找出能產生該摘要的原始輸入。
Second Preimage Resistance：已知一份資料，難以找到另一份不同資料產生相同摘要。

body.text: 這裡的「單向」是計算上難以逆推，不代表對短密碼或低熵輸入完全無法進行字典猜測。
4. 實際案例：攻擊者同時替換文件與 Hash
假設你從網路下載一份程式，網站也提供 SHA-256 值。
你下載後計算摘要，發現完全相同。
能否直接斷定程式安全？
不能。
如果攻擊者同時控制程式與網站公布的摘要，就可能一起替換兩者。
因此，Hash 能支援完整性檢查，但要對抗惡意竄改，還必須確保比較的摘要來源可信，或採用 HMAC、數位簽章等具有身分或金鑰驗證能力的技術。
5. 比較與區別：Hash、HMAC、Signature

items: Hash：回答「兩份資料是否相同？」
HMAC：回答「這份資料是否由掌握共享祕密金鑰的一方產生，且未被修改？」
Digital Signature：回答「是否由相對應私鑰的持有者簽署，且內容未被修改？」

body.text: HMAC 使用密碼學雜湊函數搭配祕密金鑰。NIST 明確將它定義為具金鑰的訊息認證碼。
HMAC 的限制是雙方共享同一祕密，因此通常不能像適當設計的數位簽章一樣，獨立證明究竟是哪個共享金鑰持有者產生訊息。
答案是 C. Hashing。
題幹的關鍵是 one-way function。
Symmetric Encryption 與 Asymmetric Encryption 主要是可透過適當金鑰還原的加解密機制；Encoding 則是資料表示方式的轉換，例如 Base64，不是安全雜湊。
但題目說 Hash 用來「ensure data integrity」過於簡略。正確理解應是：Hash 搭配可信比較值，可用於檢查完整性；單獨一個未受保護的摘要，不提供對抗主動攻擊者的完整性保證。
PKI：那麼誰能證明公開金鑰真的屬於對方？
假設你打開銀行網站。
攻擊者也能生成一組自己的 Public Key 和 Private Key，並宣稱自己是銀行。
因此，公開金鑰本身不等於可信任的身分。
PKI（Public Key Infrastructure，公開金鑰基礎建設）透過憑證、CA 和信任鏈等機制處理這個問題。

7. 進階補充：HTTPS 不只是加密
TLS 1.3 的常見憑證式連線，結合了 ECDHE 金鑰建立、憑證與簽章驗證、金鑰導出，以及 AEAD 對稱加密。
因此，一條真正受保護的連線通常需要同時考慮機密性（Confidentiality）、完整性（Integrity）及身分驗證（Authentication）。
只有加密而沒有適當的身分驗證，可能仍遭遇中間人攻擊；只有 Hash 而沒有受保護的驗證方式，也不能保證資料沒有遭到有意竄改。

情境 1
一家醫院授權你測試兩個指定 API。你發現第三個由外包商管理的 API 可能有高風險漏洞，但不在合約範圍內。最適當的行動是什麼？
A. 立即測試，因為發現漏洞可以保護病人
B. 暫停對該 API 的主動測試，請求確認或擴充授權
C. 只要不用破壞性工具，就可以先測試
D. 請另一位研究員測試，就不算違反自己的授權
情境 2
醫院要建立風險評估方法、處理 SOC 警報，以及制定重大災難期間的診療作業計畫。哪一組配對最符合各項工作的目的？
A. ISO 27002／Tier 3／SLA
B. ISO 27005／Tier 1／BCP
C. ISO 27701／SOC Manager／NDA
D. ISO 27001／Incident Commander／AUP
情境 3
一台存有敏感病歷的 SSD 即將交給外部回收商。磁碟曾加密，但目前無法確認是否有未加密區域或外部金鑰副本。最佳做法是什麼？
A. 刪除所有檔案並清空垃圾桶
B. 只要執行金鑰刪除就必然達到 Purge
C. 確認加密涵蓋範圍與媒體特性，採合適清除方法並驗證留證
D. 直接交給回收商，因為 SSD 難以復原
情境 4
某系統使用 64-bit 區塊加密演算法，金鑰為 256 bits，且持續在同一金鑰下處理大量資料。最值得優先進一步評估的是什麼？
A. 256-bit 金鑰代表不存在任何加密風險
B. 所有安全問題都只能由暴力破解造成
C. 區塊長度、運作模式與資料量可能造成生日界限相關風險
D. 把金鑰增加到 448 bits 就能保證解決所有問題
情境 5
一家企業 API 會將資料及其 SHA-256 值傳送給客戶，但攻擊者有機會同時修改兩者。企業另外使用 HTTPS，但客戶端未正確驗證伺服器憑證。哪項改善最合適？
A. 將 SHA-256 改為 Base64
B. 正確驗證 TLS 伺服器身分，並依需求採用經驗證的完整性保護機制
C. 將 SHA-256 重複計算十次即可解決身分驗證問題
D. 只提高資料壓縮率，避免攻擊者辨認內容
這次課程要建立的核心能力，是從題目描述辨識出真正的安全目標、所使用的技術，以及安全保證成立的必要條件。能夠做到這三件事，就不只是記住九個答案，而是具備分析更多 CEH 題目的基礎。

en.title: Part 2 | M01 × M20: governance, sanitization, encryption and certificate trust

sections.heading: Build a security knowledge map

body.text: This is part 2 of the dated set: nine references spanning M01 foundations and M20 cryptography. Understand the security problem before selecting a technology, role or management system; recognizing English words is only the starting point.

items: Permission: valid authorization and testing boundaries.
Risk assessment: assessing information-security risk.
Laboratory-grade recovery: the recovery capability addressed by purge.
64-bit block: block size, not key length.
One-way function: hashing, not reversible encryption.
Issuing and signing certificates: the responsibility of a CA.

body.text: 1. Why does security need multiple technologies?

Imagine managing hospital security: doctors log into records, patients access information online and the hospital commissions regular vulnerability tests. The issues include authorization, risk, monitoring, continuity, sanitization, encryption and trust, rather than only whether an intrusion occurred. The source’s “seven hospital security questions” diagram did not include its detailed nodes in the supplied text; the supplied five-unit table below carries the available knowledge structure.

rows: What permits testing another party’s system?
How do we prevent issues, detect attacks and continue operating?
How does deletion differ from secure sanitization?
How do we protect data and establish keys securely?
Has data changed, and is the website identity trusted?

body.text: 2. Connect the protection goals through CIA

body.name: cia
body.caption: CIA: three information-security objectives
body.description: These are fundamental information-security objectives used by NIST. The three columns are parallel objectives, not sequential steps.

items.title: C · Confidentiality
items.body:
Confidentiality
People without permission must not see the data

items.title: I · Integrity
items.body:
Integrity
Data must remain correct and trustworthy

items.title: A · Availability
items.body:
Availability
Usable when needed

body.text: Confidentiality means patient B cannot freely inspect patient A’s record. Integrity protects a 5 mg dose from an unauthorized change to 50 mg. Availability lets an emergency doctor obtain necessary records when needed. Strong encryption alone does not prevent ransomware from interrupting service; the five units protect CIA from different directions.

sections.heading: Unit 1 | White hats and authorization

body.text: Reference EC-Q535, connected to M01-03 ethical hacking, authorization and rules of engagement.
1. A locksmith and a thief may use the same techniques

A homeowner hires a locksmith to test a lock. The locksmith opens it with tools and recommends replacement within the agreement. Someone else opens the same lock without consent and claims merely to demonstrate insecurity. Motive alone does not establish authorization; assess the technique together with permission, purpose and conduct.
2. Understand the terminology

rows: A person exploring, analyzing or operating systems, not necessarily a criminal
Tests within lawful authorization and applicable rules
Checks exploitable weaknesses within a controlled scope
A party with authority permits specified conduct
Systems, assets and activities included in testing

body.text: ROE are more than “you may test.” An agreement might permit only test.example.com, exclude the production database, limit work to Saturday 01:00–04:00, prohibit disruptive stress testing and require immediate reporting of serious vulnerabilities to a designated contact. These are concrete boundaries.
3. The four labels do not share one classification axis

rows: May lack malicious intent but also lack authorization
Relies mainly on others’ ready-made attack tools
Describes proficiency, not an authorization category

body.text: Hat labels are not an exhaustive, mutually exclusive legal classification. A script kiddie may attack unlawfully, and an authorized tester who deliberately exceeds scope gains no exemption by calling themselves a white hat.
4. EC-Q535: permission and legal boundaries

The supplied clues are A company hires a hacker to test its network security by simulating real-world attacks and The hacker has permission and operates within legal boundaries. Has permission identifies authorization; operates within identifies a limit; legal boundaries adds the legal constraint.

rows: The question is not about technical proficiency
Malicious unlawful intrusion is not described

body.text: The supplied answer is D. Look for authorization and legality rather than guessing a role from the tool used.
5. Variation: private reporting does not replace authorization

A researcher actively tests a website without consent and later reports privately. Lack of malicious intent alone does not establish white-hat authorization. Ask whether permission exists, whether a public disclosure policy allows the specific activity and whether legal limits were exceeded. These questions demonstrate the underlying principle.

sections.heading: Unit 2 | ISO, SOC and business continuity

body.text: References P1-Q063, P3-Q086 and P3-Q088 connect understanding risk, ongoing monitoring and triage, and maintaining critical business during disruption. They work together but concern different guidance, operational responsibilities and continuity planning.
1. Risk: start with an aging hospital server

A server still works, but its old software has publicly known vulnerabilities. Ask how important it is, how likely an attack is, how severe the consequences would be and how much protection to fund. These questions begin risk management.

rows: Medical database, server, account or healthcare service
Harm to an organization when a threat exploits a weakness

body.text: The attacker is a threat; an unpatched VPN flaw is a vulnerability. Exploiting it to access records is a risk scenario, while disclosure and service interruption are impacts. Threat and vulnerability are distinct.
2. Assess and treat risk
Teaching model: Risk ≈ Likelihood × Impact. Likelihood describes how probable the event is; impact describes its consequences. Suppose a hospital uses an illustrative 1–5 scale:

rows: Serious vulnerability in an external VPN

body.text: This is not an ISO-prescribed formula or rating. Organizations define their scales, tolerance and calculation or judgment method to support prioritization, not to turn risk into a magically precise number.

items: Risk mitigation: patch, strengthen authentication or restrict access.
Risk avoidance: stop a service whose risk cannot reasonably be controlled.
Risk sharing or transfer: share part of the loss through contracts or insurance.
Risk acceptance: an appropriately authorized party accepts residual risk.

body.text: Treatment does not automatically eliminate risk, and outsourcing a system does not necessarily remove the organization’s legal or management responsibilities.

rows: How do we establish policies, responsibilities, procedures, risk management and continual improvement?
How do we identify, analyze, assess and treat information-security risk?
Which specific controls can we use as guidance?
How do we manage responsibilities for collecting, using and processing patient personal data?

body.text: Both 27005 and 27002 support 27001; they are not a mandatory sequence in which one must be completed before using the other. ISMS means information security management system; PIMS means privacy information management system. The 2025 edition of 27701 replaces the 2019 edition.
4. P1-Q063: use the verbs to identify the standard’s task

Identify, assess, and treat information security risks as part of their ISMS identifies risk identification, assessment and treatment. The question asks for specialized guidance rather than overall ISMS requirements.

rows: Privacy management, not the most direct fit
Includes risk, but specifies overall system requirements
The most direct information-security risk guidance

body.text: The supplied answer is C. If the wording changes to ISMS requirements, choose 27001; risk guidance indicates 27005, while security-controls guidance indicates 27002.
5. SOC and initial triage

A security operations center, or SOC, resembles emergency-department triage: the first line assesses urgency and routes cases needing deeper work to appropriate specialists. Senior experts cannot deeply investigate every failed-login, suspicious-connection or malware alert.

Monitoring means continuously observing activity, such as repeated administrator-login attempts. Triage assesses an alert’s importance, credibility and need for escalation. It neither proves an attack completely nor requires Tier 1 to handle every vulnerability alone.

items: False positive: an alert is confirmed not to match the suspected malicious event.
False negative: malicious activity is present but not detected.
Escalation: route a case to personnel with deeper investigative capability or appropriate authority.

body.text: An employee traveling abroad and using an approved VPN may trigger an unfamiliar-location alert without an attack. Suspicious privilege escalation, data exports and endpoint activity accompanying that login strengthen the case for investigation.
6. Other SOC roles and threat hunting

rows: Investigate, analyze incidents and assist containment
Processes, staffing, performance and escalation procedures
Coordinate major response decisions and teams

body.text: Threat hunting proactively forms hypotheses and searches for attack traces not caught by existing alerts, whereas ordinary monitoring is more like responding when an alert fires. These are typical responsibilities, not a universal organization chart. Microsoft’s SOC guidance likewise distinguishes triage, investigation and advanced threat work.

Initial monitoring and triaging of security alerts points to first-line observation and classification. The supplied answer is A, Tier 1 Analyst. B, advanced analysis; C, management; and D, major-incident command are different responsibilities. Seeing SOC alone does not justify choosing manager.
8. BCP, DRP, IRP and recovery objectives

Ransomware blocks hospital records. The team investigates, isolates and restores systems, but emergency patients have already arrived. Care operations cannot simply wait for computer repair. A business continuity plan, or BCP, addresses maintaining or resuming necessary business when systems, facilities, personnel or supply chains are disrupted.
A BCP is broader than computer repair. It may include preapproved and rehearsed alternative care workflows, emergency communications, manual records, alternative work sites and resource coordination.

rows: How does the organization continue critical services?
How are information systems and data restored?
How is the incident investigated, contained and handled?

body.text: The three plans can operate together. RTO, recovery time objective, specifies the target time to restore the required condition after interruption. RPO, recovery point objective, specifies how far back in data state recovery from copies may be tolerated.

An RTO of 2 hours targets restoring the specified system within two hours. An RPO of 15 minutes targets avoiding a rollback to a data state more than 15 minutes before the incident. Written objectives are not guarantees; backups, technical capability and exercises must support them.

Which document outlines how a business will continue to operate during and after a significant disaster? Business, continue to operate, during and after, and significant disaster point to continuity during and following disruption. The supplied answer is C, BCP.

rows: Rules for acceptable equipment or service use

body.text: ISO 22301 addresses business continuity management systems. Service levels, confidentiality commitments and usage policies are not substitutes for a business continuity plan.
10. Recall the responsibilities with three hospital questions

items: Which risks should we address first? → ISO/IEC 27005.
Who initially triages a new alert? → SOC Tier 1.
How do essential services continue during disaster? → BCP.

body.text: The same reasoning about responsibilities transfers to a school, company or financial institution.

sections.heading: Unit 3 | Deletion, purge and sanitization

body.text: Reference P3-Q110. Distinguish deletion, data recovery and media sanitization.
1. Understand deletion through a library catalog

Removing a book from a library catalog may hide it from searches while leaving it on the shelf. File deletion can similarly remove a file or reference without securely sanitizing all underlying data. Filesystems, devices, TRIM and encryption affect the result; deletion neither guarantees nor rules out recovery.
2. Why can data recovery also be a risk?

Data recovery attempts to retrieve information after accidental deletion, filesystem damage or device failure using residual content, filesystem information, backups or other copies. It helps users but creates a risk when retiring sensitive equipment. A hospital selling an old computer that held test reports cannot treat file deletion alone as satisfying sanitization requirements.
3. Clear, purge and destroy
NIST SP 800-88 Rev. 2, published in September 2025, distinguishes three media-sanitization methods.

rows: Prevent simple, noninvasive recovery through normal user interfaces
Make recovery of target data infeasible with advanced laboratory techniques while potentially preserving reuse
Sanitize contents with a higher assurance objective
Make advanced recovery infeasible and prevent the medium from storing data again

body.text: 4. Why is purge not simply smashing a drive?

Purge classifies methods and assurance objectives, not one fixed action. Suitable device-sanitization functions or reliable cryptographic erase may achieve it. If data was properly encrypted, securely eliminating all required decryption keys can remove a feasible recovery path, like removing every usable key to reliably protected contents.

items: Since the last suitable sanitization, sensitive data has been suitably encrypted without residual plaintext writes.
The cryptography and key management are reliable.
No usable key copies remain.
Unencrypted regions have not been overlooked.
The method suits the device and security requirements.

body.text: Without these conditions, pressing “delete key” does not establish successful purge.
5. Retiring a hospital SSD: device characteristics matter

Before an SSD that held medical records goes to a recycler, select a method based on sensitivity, device capabilities and intended disposition, then verify the result and retain a record. This procedural explanation is an editorial addition based on sanitization principles; the original flowchart details were not supplied in the text.

Wear leveling distributes flash writes to extend lifetime. A logical address seen by the operating system does not necessarily keep mapping to the same physical area. Ordinary file-overwriting tools therefore cannot be assumed to sanitize all original SSD data.
What is the primary purpose of a "Purge" in the data destruction process? This asks for the sanitization objective rather than subsequent hardware disposition.

rows: A. To simply delete the file pointers.
Removing references is not sufficient assurance of sanitization
B. To make data recovery impossible even with laboratory-grade tools.
Best matches purge; interpret impossible as infeasible under the specified conditions
Recycling is a possible subsequent action, not the definition
D. To archive data for 10 years.
Archiving preserves information rather than sanitizing it

body.text: The supplied answer is B. Infeasible is not an unconditional mathematical impossibility.
7. Transfer the distinction to a new scenario

If confidential data must resist advanced recovery while equipment remains available for reuse by another department, consider purge. If the requirement is actual destruction and no further use as storage, it corresponds to destroy.

sections.heading: Unit 4 | Encryption, blocks, keys and distribution

body.text: References EC-Q284 and EC-Q032 connect symmetric and asymmetric cryptography. Ask what encryption and keys are, how data is processed, and how two parties obtain a shared secret.
1. Why encrypt? The algorithm and key have different roles

Hospital A sends a test report to hospital B, which should understand it while unauthorized third parties should not. Encryption transforms plaintext into ciphertext, and decryption uses the appropriate key and related information to recover it. A simplified symmetric path is plaintext plus encryption and a secret key → ciphertext → decryption with corresponding secret material → plaintext. Real schemes also involve IVs, nonces, modes and authentication tags.

rows: Recover data using suitable keys and related information

body.text: The algorithm resembles the design of a lock; a key is the particular secret setting controlling it. Modern cryptography should remain difficult to break when an attacker knows the algorithm but lacks the necessary secret. Publishing an algorithm does not make it insecure.
2. Symmetric encryption and key distribution

Symmetric encryption uses a shared secret key or corresponding secret material. It resembles encrypting with a common password that a colleague also uses to decrypt. It is usually efficient for databases, storage and large network transfers. But parties without an existing shared secret cannot safely send a key over an unprotected channel; that is the key-distribution problem.
3. Bit, byte, block and key size

A bit is 0 or 1; a byte is normally 8 bits. Thus 64 bits = 8 bytes and 128 bits = 16 bytes. A block is a fixed data unit transformed by a block cipher, while block size measures that unit in bits. Key size measures key length, a separate quantity.

An algorithm transforming 8 bytes at a time has a 64-bit block. An 8,000-byte file requires a suitable mode to process units and handle the final portion; the entire file is not limited to one block. Blowfish retains a 64-bit block regardless of its 32–448-bit key choice, while AES uses 128-bit blocks.
As an analogy, block size is the amount a machine processes at once, while key size relates to the number of possible secret settings. Both matter; the analogy only distinguishes their roles.
4. Block cipher and stream cipher

Block ciphers transform fixed-length blocks, as AES, Blowfish and Twofish do. Stream ciphers process data using mechanisms such as a keystream; RC4 and ChaCha20 are examples. An explicit 64-bit blocks clue calls for a matching block cipher rather than a stream cipher.
5. Specifications of four algorithms

Bruce Schneier introduced Blowfish in 1993; its design page documents 64-bit blocks and 32–448-bit keys. Twofish uses 128-bit blocks. NIST FIPS 197 specifies three AES key lengths, all with the same 128-bit block size.
6. EC-Q284: find the most discriminating clues

The financial company, disclosure, intercepted ciphertext and secure storage are background. The decisive clues are processes data in 64-bit blocks and supports a variable key size from 32 to 448 bits.

items: RC4 is a stream cipher; exclude it.
Twofish uses 128-bit blocks; exclude it.
AES has 128-bit blocks and not a 32–448-bit key range; exclude it.
Blowfish matches both clues; the supplied answer is D.

body.text: Being a DES alternative is plausible historical context, not a unique identifier. Actual ciphertext alone usually does not reveal the algorithm automatically; protocol negotiation, configuration or file-format evidence may be needed.
7. A longer key does not guarantee a safer system

A uniformly random 128-bit key has 2^128 possibilities. Each extra bit doubles the search space for brute force. Security also depends on blocks, modes, mathematical weaknesses, key generation and implementation, so comparing Blowfish 448 with AES 256 alone is insufficient.
8. The birthday bound and 64-bit blocks

Although there are 365 possible birthdays, 23 people already give approximately a greater-than-50% chance of a shared birthday. This birthday paradox illustrates why collisions matter. Under some modes, processing around 2^32 64-bit blocks with one key demands particular care.

At 8 bytes per block, 2^32 × 8 bytes = 34,359,738,368 bytes, approximately 34.4 GB or 32 GiB. Crossing that amount does not guarantee immediate disclosure; modes, key use and other attack conditions matter. Sweet32 in 2016 demonstrated attacks under particular TLS/OpenVPN and CBC conditions, not a universal fixed safe volume for all encryption.

A mode of operation specifies how to use a block cipher for longer messages; examples include CBC, CTR and GCM. AEAD, authenticated encryption with associated data, combines confidentiality with integrity and authentication of associated data when used correctly. AES is the core cipher; AES-GCM is a scheme using a particular mode. A long Blowfish key does not remove its small-block limitations.
9. Public/private keys, ECDHE and KDFs

Asymmetric cryptography uses mathematically related public and private keys. The public key can be shared; the private key must be protected. In a public-key encryption scheme, Alice can encrypt using Bob’s trusted public key and Bob can decrypt with his private key. Not every asymmetric algorithm encrypts documents, and this does not imply directly processing large files that way.

ECDHE, ephemeral elliptic-curve Diffie–Hellman, lets both parties exchange public information and locally compute a shared secret without transmitting that secret directly. This is key agreement. A key derivation function, or KDF, derives session keys, which symmetric mechanisms use to protect bulk data.

A common hybrid division is public-key mechanisms establish secret material → a KDF derives keys → symmetric mechanisms protect data. Symmetric cryptography is generally better suited to bulk data, while public-key mechanisms handle key establishment and signatures rather than directly encrypting everything.
10. EC-Q032: key distribution
Which encryption method supports secure key distribution? Identify the category that best supports establishing keys securely.

rows: A storage-protection use case rather than the typical initial key-distribution principle
Needs an existing shared secret; it can protect other keys, such as through key wrapping, under existing management, but is not the most direct answer here
A digest alone does not establish a secure shared secret
The best match among the four options

body.text: The supplied answer is D. A real design must specify the actual protocol and authentication. Establishing a secret does not identify the peer: a man in the middle can replace public values and establish separate secrets with the two endpoints. Key establishment therefore needs trusted authentication, leading to PKI and CAs.

sections.heading: Unit 5 | Hashes, signatures, PKI and CAs

body.text: References P3-Q074 and P3-Q121 distinguish checking whether content changed from checking whether its source is genuine. The two questions require different evidence.
1. Hash: a fixed-length digital fingerprint

Hashing resembles a machine calculating a fixed-length fingerprint from document content. The hash function produces a hash value, digest or message digest. SHA-256 outputs 256 bits for a short text or any file size within its permitted input range.

body.name: hash
body.caption: Different content usually produces different hashes
body.description: The two inputs are compared in parallel. Digest A/B are conceptual labels, not computed SHA-256 results. Collisions exist mathematically; security requires that exploitable collisions be difficult to find.

items.title: Input A
items.body:
Patient blood pressure: 120
↓ SHA-256
Produces digest A

items.title: Input B
items.body:
Patient blood pressure: 180
↓ SHA-256
Produces digest B, usually different from A

body.text: Changing one character usually changes the output substantially, but hashes are not unique for every possible input. More possible inputs than fixed-length outputs means collisions must exist. Secure hashing requires that exploitable collisions be difficult to find, along with properties such as one-way behavior.
2. One-way does not mean inputs cannot be guessed

A one-way function is easy to compute from input to digest but difficult to invert from digest to original. Encryption has a decryption procedure for appropriate key holders; hashing is not designed to decrypt a digest.

body.name: compare
body.caption: Encryption and hashing have different directions
body.description: Encryption has a corresponding decryption procedure; hashing has no decryption operation. Low-entropy inputs can still be guessed and hashed for comparison. That is guessing an input, not decrypting a digest.

items.title: Encryption
items.body:
Plaintext
↓ Algorithm and key
Ciphertext
↑ The appropriate key can recover the plaintext

items.title: Hashing
items.body:
Original data
↓ Hash function
Digest
No corresponding decryption operation

body.text: If a password comes from a small set such as 1234 or 0000, an attacker can hash candidates and compare them. That is guessing the input, not reverse decryption.
3. Conditions for checking changes with a hash

A hospital provides a report’s SHA-256 through a trusted channel. Recalculate it after receiving the file. A mismatch indicates different data or computation conditions; a match provides strong consistency evidence under the security assumptions and trusted-reference condition. Hashing does not prevent modification. If an attacker replaces both the document and the posted digest, comparison alone may miss the attack.
4. HMAC: authentication using a shared secret

HMAC, hash-based message authentication code, combines a hash with a shared secret key. Anyone can compute an ordinary hash; generating a valid HMAC requires secret material. Hospital A calculates it with a shared key and hospital B verifies with that key. An attacker lacking the key cannot simply change the data and recompute an ordinary hash to produce a valid HMAC.

NIST FIPS 198-1 describes this definition; its website also notes a plan to move the content to SP 800-224. Both holders of the shared key can generate HMACs, so an HMAC alone does not identify which holder sent a message. This differs from a publicly verifiable signature.
5. Digital signature: private-key signing and public-key verification

A digital signature provides integrity and evidence associated with the private key corresponding to a public key. Conceptually, data undergoes the scheme’s hashing/encoding and private-key signing, then travels with the signature. A receiver verifies using the trusted public key and specified scheme. Details depend on the algorithm; signing is not generically encrypting a hash with a private key.

rows: Encrypt with the recipient’s public key; decrypt with the recipient’s private key
Sign with the signer’s private key; verify with the corresponding public key

body.text: If the public key’s identity is unknown, mathematical verification does not establish the real-world signer. Key and identity management remain necessary.
6. P3-Q074 and encoding
Which of the following is a "one-way" function used to ensure data integrity? One-way, function and data integrity indicate hashing.

rows: Has encryption/decryption, not the requested one-way digest
Public-key encryption, not this digest function
A representation, not equivalent to cryptographic hashing or encryption

body.text: The supplied answer is C. Base64 represents binary data as text for transmission or storage. Anyone can decode it using public rules; it does not provide confidentiality.
7. PKI: possessing a public key is insufficient

An attacker can generate a key pair and claim, just as a bank does, “This is my public key.” A system is needed to bind keys to identities or domains through trusted processes. PKI, public key infrastructure, includes certificates, CAs, trust anchors and management/validation procedures.
8. CA: the certificate issuer

A CA, certificate authority, resembles a credential issuer. A company applies for a website certificate; the CA validates information under its policy and issues it. The certificate includes the public key, applicable identity information, validity, issuer and signature. The CA signature lets a browser validate the issuing chain under its trust policy.
9. Certificate chain: from root to website

rows: An intermediate authorized by an issuer above it
Website public key and domain-related information

body.text: Browsers or operating systems maintain trusted root sets in common Web PKI, and actual chains vary in depth. Validation checks more than a CA signature: chain, name, validity, purpose and constraints matter. A publicly trusted certificate does not guarantee lawful business conduct, safe content or absence of malware. Its trust concerns the specified identity/key relationship.
10. How does HTTPS combine the mechanisms?

HTTPS is HTTP protected by TLS. Common certificate-based TLS 1.3 combines asymmetric key establishment such as ECDHE, CA certificates and server authentication, key derivation and symmetric AEAD such as AES-GCM. The following preserves endpoints, message directions and local validation responsibilities.

body.caption: TLS 1.3: simplified certificate-based ECDHE exchange
body.description: Solid arrows mean browser-to-server messages; dashed arrows mean server replies, not unencrypted traffic. Orange boxes indicate local computation or validation. EncryptedExtensions, key-schedule details, client certificates and other branches are omitted; this is not a packet capture. Server handshake messages from Certificate onward are protected with handshake keys.

items.body: The browser offers supported parameters and a public key share.

In a "Public Key Infrastructure" (PKI), who is responsible for issuing and signing digital certificates? Issuing and signing are different from validating a certificate during a connection.

Being an ISP does not automatically make an entity a CA

cards.question: Is attack-tool ability the main difference between white and black hats?

cards.question: How do ISO/IEC 27001, 27002 and 27005 differ?
